title: Pontotoc’s boys pose with their state banner. Three relay teams earned 44 of their 85 points
excerpt: The Warriors tied Pearl River Central for the Class II swimming title. A freestyle relay win and two more relay podium finishes supplied over half of Pontotoc’s points.
locality: Pontotoc City School District, with state swimming finals at the Tupelo Aquatic Center.

facts.statement: Pontotoc’s boys swim team gathered behind a red state championship banner, with the trophy on the grass in front of them, in photos the school district shared Friday. The state meet results tell how close that title was. Pontotoc and Pearl River Central finished with 85 points apiece, and three relays supplied 44 of the Warriors’ points.

paragraphs.text: Pontotoc’s boys swim team gathered behind a red state championship banner, with the trophy on the grass in front of them, in photos the school district shared Friday. The state meet results tell how close that title was. Pontotoc and Pearl River Central finished with 85 points apiece, and three relays supplied 44 of the Warriors’ points.

The Warriors’ relay win came in the 200-yard freestyle at the Oct. 17 finals in Tupelo. Carson Poynor, Cason Cruse, Elijah Farris and Thomas Jefcoat finished in 1:39.87, nearly three seconds ahead of runner-up Warren Central. The win was worth 18 points. Pearl River Central finished fourth and earned 10.

Jefcoat and Poynor also swam the 200 medley relay with Jett Pollard and Liam Rackley. They took second in 1:58.75, just under half a second ahead of Warren Central’s 1:59.22. Pearl River Central won that event in 1:53.16.

The two teams went into the last boys relay six points apart. Pearl River Central won the 400 freestyle for 18 points. Cruse, Jake Cooley, Farris and Rackley finished third for Pontotoc in 3:57.55, earning the 12 points that left the teams level. West Jones finished third in the team standings with 77½.

image.alt_text: Pontotoc earned 14 points in the 200 medley relay, 18 in the 200 freestyle and 12 in the 400 freestyle in its 85-point state championship tie.
